subject: Dealing with errors generated by package functions in a more elegant way.

messages.author: 3bf225a8a5f5becd
messages.subject: Dealing with errors generated by package functions in a more elegant way.
parts:
Hi all,

Our department also discovered Shiny, so we're using it more and more as an interface to packages we develop here. Many upsides, but we experience a very serious downside as well:

The packages we develop, contain a whole set of checks and informative error messages to catch every mistake a silly user can make. But when creating an interface to these packages, all those checks become useless:

- the errors aren't conveniently displayed in the app.
- more seriously, errors just stop the app from running when deployed over the server and accessed through a web browser.

I am familiar with need() and validate(), but reimplementing all checks we have in the package in the app seems like a lot of redundant work. Right now we succeed by wrapping everything in tryCatch(), and using this to catch a possible error message for redirection to a verbatim display. This works, but it still feels bulky and unnecessary complicated.

Is there a way to graciously redirect stderr to any kind of output, and prevent the app from stopping with every error it occurs?

Thank you in advance.
Cheers
Joris
